parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> BeanWave Coffee (BWC) is a small roaster in country L. It buys green coffee beans from Brazil and pays in US dollars (USD). BWC sells roasted coffee to local cafés. The owner is considering buying a new semi-automatic roasting machine to improve quality and reduce roasting time. The machine costs L\$150 000. Staff would need training. Packaging is currently non-recyclable, and energy costs are rising.
> 
> **Table 1.1 – Exchange rate change and recent invoice**
> 
> | Item | Value |
> |---|---|
> | Last month’s bean invoice | **USD 12 000** |
> | Exchange rate before | **1 USD = L\$4.5** |
> | Exchange rate now | **1 USD = L\$5.0** |

Explain **two** possible disadvantages to BWC of buying the new roasting machine.
parts.solution_md:
The high upfront cost **[K] **of L\$150 000 **[Ap]** could strain cash, leading to less money for marketing or buying beans, which risks stock shortages and lost sales **[An]**

Training will be needed and disruption **[K] **is likely to occur because staff must learn the new machine **[Ap]**, so output may slow at first, reducing short-term capacity and increasing average costs **[An]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Write two developed paragraphs, one for each part of the question
> - For **each paragraph**:
> 
>   - State a valid point relevant to the question → 1 K mark
>   - Apply each point clearly to the stimulus → 1 Ap mark
>   - Explain the impact using a cause–effect chain → 1 An mark
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Purchase/maintenance costs are likely to increase → cash flow pressure/interest costs [an]
>   - Risk the machine doesn’t improve quality as expected [an]
>   - Obsolescence/technology risk; energy use when costs are rising [ap][an]
>   - Opportunity cost: money not used for recyclable packaging switch [ap][an]

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Playsafe Playground Equipment (PPE)**

Kaari has always been creative and made wooden toys for her two children when they were young. Her children are now at school, so Kaari decided to start her own business making wooden playground equipment.

Kaari started PPE as a sole trader business three years ago in country Z. She wants an income from the business but also wants to spend time with her children. Kaari wants the business to remain small. However, if the business grows Kaari may need to change to another type of business organisation. Kaari carries out all the management roles in the business.

Kaari uses job production to produce high quality, individually designed playground equipment. Kaari designs all the equipment herself and she employs 3 skilled workers to help her make the products. PPE currently makes both large and small items of playground equipment each week.

Kaari uses cost-plus pricing as every item of playground equipment uses different quantities of raw materials. She sells small items of playground equipment to retailers and large items of playground equipment to the Government. There are many competitors in this market.

Kaari plans to obtain new machinery which will cost \$20 000. She is considering using crowd-funding as this is one way to raise capital for new business investment. Other options include leasing the machinery or asking the bank for a loan.

Kaari has developed a new unique product this year. There are no other similar products in the market.

**Appendix 1**

**Advertisement for PPE**

Buy your playground equipment from us.

At PPE we manufacture high quality playground equipment and have better designs than our competitors.

All our equipment has been fully tested and is guaranteed to meet legal safety standards. We are the main supplier of playground equipment to the Government for public parks - so you know our equipment can be trusted!

Contact us today for a price list.

**Appendix 2**

**Cost and revenue information for PPE in 2021**

|   | **Small item of playgroundequipment** | **Large item of playgroundequipment** |
|---|---|---|
| Average selling price | \$100 | \$1 000 |
| Average cost of manufacture | \$25 | \$500 |
| Output each week | 15 | 3 |

**Appendix 3**

**Newspaper article – Main News 1st October 2021**

**Children need to get more exercise and play outside**

Research suggests that playing outside helps children relax after school and improves their health.

The Government in country Z has allocated \$10m to spend on improving children’s playgrounds in public places. This means there will be \$5 000 to spend on equipment for each public playground.

Retailers have reported increasing demand for small items of playground equipment as parents want to have these products at home. This trend is expected to continue.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages to PPE of investing in the following **three** types of technology to improve their manufacturing process:

- Automated cutting machinery
- Computer-aided design (CAD) software
- Quality control sensors

Which technology investment should PPE prioritise? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following[ insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2021-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Automated cutting machinery would increase production speed and precision for PPE's playground equipment **[Ap]**, reducing labour costs with only 3 employees. However, the high initial cost of \$\$20,000 could strain cash flow **[Ap]**, and Kaari may need training to operate complex machinery **[An]**

CAD software would enable Kaari to create more innovative playground designs digitally **[Ap]**, allowing faster prototyping and easier modifications for customer requirements. The software could help PPE compete with larger manufacturers through superior design capabilities **[Ap]**. However, Kaari would need time to learn the software, potentially slowing initial production **[An]**

Quality control sensors would ensure consistent product standards, reducing defects and potential safety issues with playground equipment **[Ap]**. This could enhance PPE's reputation and reduce warranty costs. However, sensors require ongoing maintenance and calibration **[An]**, adding operational complexity for a small business **[An]**

PPE should prioritise CAD software investment **[E]**. As a design-focused business, superior playground equipment designs would differentiate PPE from competitors **[Ap]** and justify premium pricing **[E]**. Unlike machinery or sensors, CAD software has lower ongoing costs and immediate impact on product development **[E]**. The other technologies could be considered later once revenue increases from improved designs **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the technology benefit/drawback
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
>   - Add a final Evaluation (E):
>   
>     - Decide which technology offers best return on investment
>     - Justify your choice
>     - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Automated cutting machinery**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Faster production speeds → increased output capacity
>     - Precise cuts reduce material waste → lower production costs
>     - Consistent quality → fewer defects and returns
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - High capital cost of \$\$20,000 → significant cash flow impact
>     - Requires operator training → temporary productivity loss
>     - Maintenance costs → ongoing operational expenses
> - **CAD software**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Enhanced design capabilities → competitive advantage through innovation
>     - Faster prototyping → quicker response to customer needs
>     - Digital storage and modification → improved efficiency
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Learning curve required → initial productivity reduction
>     - Subscription costs → ongoing expense
>     - Requires computer hardware upgrades → additional investment
> - **Quality control sensors**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Consistent product standards → reduced defect rates
>     - Early problem detection → prevents costly recalls
>     - Enhanced safety compliance → protects brand reputation
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Ongoing calibration needs → maintenance complexity
>     - Technical expertise required → training or hiring costs
>     - False readings possible → potential production disruption
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - CAD software offers immediate design improvements with manageable costs and learning requirements
>   - Automated machinery provides long-term efficiency but requires substantial upfront investment
>   - Quality sensors enhance standards but add operational complexity for small business
>   - PPE should prioritise technology that maximises competitive advantage while managing cash flow constraints

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

**Soapy Sudds Manufacturer (SSM)**

SSM is a public limited company that was set up 25 years ago. SSM manufacture soap powder in country Y. The soap powder is used for washing clothes. SSM sells all its soap powder to large retailers in country Y. SSM’s sales have been increasing for many years in country Y but sales in the last year have remained the same. The directors of SSM are considering ways to increase sales.

SSM has a total of 100 employees with 60 in the Operations Department. It uses flow production in the factory and has 10 production lines with 5 workers and 1 supervisor for each line. The Operations Manager is aware that production workers are unhappy and often complain about their jobs being boring. These workers have always been paid by an hourly rate. The Human Resources Manager has recommended changes to ensure fewer workers leave each year to work for other businesses.

The directors of SSM have decided to expand the factory. They will need \$15m to do this. The directors have also considered taking over a competitor. SSM is likely to benefit from economies of scale as it grows.

The Marketing Director thinks SSM should start selling soap powder in markets in other countries. SSM will need to carry out either primary market research or secondary market research to forecast the potential total sales in these new markets. There are many existing manufacturers in these countries. SSM need to consider the problems when entering new markets in other countries such as tariffs or quotas.

**Appendix 1**

**Manufacturing process to make soap powder**

All the different types of soap powder are manufactured on production lines using flow production. SSM makes use of specialisation.

Each production line has the following stages:

![Flowchart of soap powder production: Stage 1 - raw materials mixed; Stage 2 - released onto conveyor belt; Stage 3 - packaged; Stage 4 - quality checks; Stage 5 - stored.](assets/001-flowchart-of-soap-powder-production-stage-1-raw-.png)

Each of these stages uses machinery controlled by a production worker

Appendix 2

Email from the SSM Finance Director to the Managing Director

SSM has a cash-flow problem which may get worse. Please see charts below

![Two bar graphs comparing days taken to pay SSM (left) and SSM paying suppliers (right) from 2019 to 2021. Both graphs show increasing trends.](assets/002-two-bar-graphs-comparing-days-taken-to-pay-ssm-l.png)

**Appendix 3**

**Newspaper article from Main News 1 October 2021**

Retailers have reported increased sales for most types of products such as sales of washing machines which have increased by 15%. Economic growth in country Y is predicted to increase.

Many businesses have been recruiting additional employees and there are now shortages of some skilled workers. The government in country Y has recorded an increase in inflation to 8% so far this year, which is a worry.

Consider how SSM could benefit from implementing the following three types of technology in production.

- Automation technology
- Digital monitoring systems
- Artificial intelligence (AI) in quality control

Which technology implementation is likely to have the greatest effect on SSM? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following [insert](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2021-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf) when answering the question.
parts.solution_md:
Automation technology would allow SSM to replace manual labour with robotic systems in the soap powder production process **[Ap]**. This would reduce labour costs and could help address the high labour turnover issues **[Ap]** as fewer workers would be needed **[An]**

Digital monitoring systems would enable SSM to track production efficiency and equipment performance in real-time, identifying bottlenecks and maintenance needs **[An]**. This would reduce downtime and improve the consistency of soap powder quality **[Ap]**

Artificial intelligence in quality control would allow SSM to detect defects and inconsistencies automatically during production. AI systems can analyse product quality faster and more accurately than human inspectors **[An]**, reducing waste and improving customer satisfaction **[Ap]**

Automation technology is likely to have the greatest effect on SSM **[E]**. As a manufacturer using flow production **[Ap]** with high labour turnover problems, automation would provide the most significant long-term benefits. It would reduce dependency on human workers and eliminate recruitment and training costs **[Ap]**. While digital monitoring would improve efficiency, it still requires skilled operators **[E]**. AI quality control would reduce waste, but automation addresses SSM's fundamental staffing challenges whilst also reducing variable costs permanently **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the technology benefit
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
>   - Add a final Evaluation (E):
>   
>     - Decide which technology has the greatest impact
>     - Justify your choice
>     - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Automation technology**
> 
>   - Robotic systems replace manual workers → reduced labour costs → lower variable cost per unit
>   - Eliminates recruitment and training costs associated with high staff turnover
> - **Digital monitoring systems**
> 
>   - Real-time tracking of production efficiency → identifies equipment issues early
>   - Reduces downtime and improves consistency of soap powder quality
> - **AI quality control**
> 
>   - Automated defect detection → faster and more accurate than human inspection
>   - Reduces waste and improves customer satisfaction through consistent quality
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Automation: provides the biggest long-term impact by addressing SSM's labour turnover problems whilst permanently reducing variable costs in large-scale production
>   - Digital monitoring: improves efficiency but requires skilled operators, so impact depends on staff availability
>   - AI quality control: reduces waste but doesn't solve fundamental staffing issues, making its effect more limited than automation

parts.problem_md: Do you think new technology in production always improves quality? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
On the positive side, technology can reduce human error and increase precision **[K]** by using automated systems and sensors, which means products are more consistent and meet quality standards more reliably **[An]**

Technology can also enable better monitoring and testing throughout production **[K]** leading to early detection of defects and higher overall product quality **[An]**

However, new technology can sometimes introduce new types of problems, such as software glitches or machine malfunctions **[K]** which could result in defective products or production delays that affect quality **[An]**

Overall, whether technology improves quality depends on how well it is implemented and maintained. Well-designed and properly maintained technology systems are more likely to improve quality **[E]** while poorly implemented or outdated technology may actually harm quality. Given these mixed outcomes, businesses should focus on careful planning, staff training, and regular maintenance when introducing new production technology. This approach helps ensure that technological advances genuinely improve rather than compromise product quality **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps improve quality (cause-effect chain) → 1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also affect quality → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Reduces human error / increases precision [k] leading to more consistent products [an]
>   - Better monitoring and testing systems [k] so defects detected earlier [an]
>   - Automated quality control [k] so higher standards maintained [an]
>   - Software glitches / machine malfunctions [k] so defective products produced [an]
>   - Complex technology requires skilled operators [k] so quality may suffer if staff not properly trained [an]
>   - High initial costs [k] leading to pressure to cut corners elsewhere affecting quality [an]
>   - Technology becomes outdated quickly [k] so quality improvements may be temporary [an]
>   - Other appropriate responses should also be credited
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - Technology can reduce errors [k] leading to better quality products [an]. However, complex systems can malfunction [k] causing quality problems [an]. No, technology does not always improve quality as it depends on implementation and maintenance. Well-managed technology improves quality [eval] whereas poorly implemented systems can make quality worse [eval]
> - The answer must focus on quality improvements or problems so do not accept points such as 'faster production' or 'lower costs' unless clearly linked to quality issues

**The BB Health Spa (BB)**

Bethany owns The BB Health Spa in Main City in country X. Economic growth has been high for the last few years. The government of country X wants this growth to continue so it has reduced income tax. However, it is also worried about inflation becoming a problem so it has increased interest rates.

The BB Health Spa is very busy and Bethany is considering taking on a partner to help manage the business and give her more free time. However, she has been a sole trader for 10 years and wants the business to stay small.

The customers of The BB Health Spa are people of all ages who are interested in their health. Bethany employs two qualified workers to provide the treatments for customers. Bethany herself also provides customers with treatments. In addition, she does all the administration such as ordering inventory, accounts and paying invoices when the spa is closed.

The BB Health Spa still uses the original treatment equipment which was purchased when the business started. Some spas nearby have the latest equipment but these spas charge much higher prices than The BB Health Spa. Bethany records all the financial transactions by filling in accounts books by hand. This takes her a long time. Customers book appointments using the telephone and Bethany later telephones them to remind them when an appointment is due.

**Appendix 1**

**Advert for treatments at The BB Health Spa**

![Flyer for The BB Health Spa including a massage room, gym equipment, and people doing yoga. Services listed: Sports Therapies, Gym, and Yoga.](assets/003-flyer-for-the-bb-health-spa-including-a-massage-.png)

**Appendix 2**

**Weekly forecasts for two possible additional services**

|   | Steam room | Hair cuts |
|---|---|---|
| Additional customers | 200 | 50 |
| Average price charged per customer | \$5 | \$25 |
| Wages | \$60 | \$400 |
| Cost of sales | \$40 | \$125 |
| Lease of equipment | \$400 | \$175 |

**Appendix 3**

**Daily News                                                                                                            September**

**New equipment now available in many health spas to make skin look younger**

There have been a number of changes in technology for health spas which allow the treatments to be much more effective in making skin look younger. Many people are keen to try these treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. This equipment is very expensive for health spas to buy or lease.

The news of these treatments has appeared on social media sites and on mobile phone Apps leading to higher demand. ‘Some customers will pay high prices for such treatments’, said a local health spa owner who is keen to promote his health spa as being one of the first to use the new equipment.

There have also been developments in software which make customer bookings and accounts much easier, quicker and with fewer mistakes. Automatic text (sms) messages are used to remind customers of their appointments – so no need to miss an appointment again.

Look out for these changes in health spas near you!

**Explain** **two **advantages and **two **disadvantages for employees of the new technology identified in Appendix 3.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-01-specimen-2020-paper-2-insert-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question

Automated booking software reduces employee workload **[K]**. Staff no longer need to manually write down appointments, which saves time **[Ap]**

New treatment equipment makes employees' jobs easier **[K]**. Staff can provide better quality treatments with less physical effort required **[Ap]**

Employees may need training to use new technology **[K]**. This could cause stress and anxiety for staff who are not confident with technology **[Ap]**

New technology might lead to job losses **[K]**. Automated systems could replace some employee roles, making staff redundant **[Ap]**

>   - improved working conditions – technology can reduce physical strain
>   - better customer service – technology helps staff provide improved service
>

parts.problem_md:
> **[case-study]**
> TYA is a limited company which manufactures 300 000 cars a year. It has 600 employees. TYA has high fixed costs. The Managing Director wants to improve efficiency in the factory. He said: ‘Globalisation is changing how businesses operate. Many manufacturing businesses are considering whether to relocate their operations to other countries.’

Explain **two **methods TYA could use to increase efficiency.
parts.solution_md:
TYA could introduce automation in its factory** [K]**. This would allow the company to produce cars faster and potentially reduce labour costs **[An] **among its 600 employees** [Ap]**. Automation could involve using robots or computer-controlled machinery on the production line. This may help TYA lower its high fixed costs over time** [An]**

Another method is implementing just-in-time inventory control **[K]**. This lean production technique would reduce the amount of parts and materials stored in TYA's factory **[An]**. With less inventory, TYA could use its factory space more efficiently to manufacture its 300,000 cars per year **[Ap]**, which may reduce its high fixed costs **[An]**

parts.problem_md: Do you think the ways technology has changed production methods benefit all employees? **Justify **your answer.
parts.solution_md:
On the positive side, technology can make jobs safer and more enjoyable **[K] **by automating dangerous tasks, which means employees are less likely to be injured at work.  It also creates opportunities for workers to learn new skills, which may open up opportunities for promotion, leading to higher pay **[An]**

However, some workers may find that their jobs become repetitive, reducing their job satisfaction, and some may even lose their jobs **[K]** as machines take over, leading to unemployment and lower living standards **[An]**

Overall, whether an employee benefits depends on their ability to adapt. Workers who gain new technical skills are more likely to benefit, while those unable to adjust often struggle **[E]**. Given these mixed impacts, businesses should focus on helping all employees transition as technology changes production. This could include retraining programmes and gradually introducing new technologies. With the right approach, the benefits of new production methods can be more widely shared **[E]**
